patterns.comment: table row: any line carrying a divider, claimed before the line rules below because a row's first cell now opens the line rather than sitting behind a border. The pipes (and any stray dashes/crosses) share the separator's quiet chrome colour so all table symbols read alike, upright; cell text falls to cell-safe shapes and the extension's semantic tokens overlay the parsed truth (attribute / Example / value / formula)

table rule: the '---+---' line an older file (before 1.12) drew under its header. It marks nothing now — the header is the row that stands first — and the next re-draw takes it out; until then every symbol is chrome, one quiet colour. Two symbols at least, so a lone '-' stays the Example whose name is still being typed. Punctuation, not comment: comment scopes render italic in most themes, and an italic pipe tilts
patterns.name: punctuation.definition.table.aot

patterns.comment: Concept: a type / class, the structural backbone. A quote ends the name, but an apostrophe inside a word is a letter of it — 'Aristotle's Ethics' is one name, so a ' followed by a letter is consumed rather than closing the run
patterns.name: entity.name.type.concept.aot
